messages.content: Baltimore update: the Wednesday 9:00 meeting and Thursday debrief are both staying by the central library. The afternoon partner visit moved farther east, but the host said they can send a rideshare from the morning site. Can we compare the library-area room they held with the Hampton Inner Harbor before I finalize airfare?
Yes. I can compare them around the actual movement pattern now. Do you have the library hotel name, total, and hold deadline?

It is Hotel Revival near Mount Vernon. Standard queen, refundable, about $438 total for Feb. 22-24. No breakfast included. The courtesy hold expires tomorrow at 6 p.m. Hampton Inner Harbor is now showing $316 total, standard king, breakfast included.

Here is the practical comparison:

| Option | 2-night total | 9:00 library meeting | Afternoon east visit | Breakfast / room basics | Bed / dining | Cancellation / flight effect |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hotel Revival / library area | ~$438 | Easiest: about a 4-6 min walk | No real advantage now, since host rideshare starts from the library | No included breakfast; coffee listed; fridge/mini-fridge needs confirmation | Standard queen; on-site restaurant/bar, good for dinner | Hold expires tomorrow 6 p.m.; if Thursday debrief runs late, this gives the most margin for a 2:40-ish BWI return |
| Hampton Inner Harbor | ~$316 | Still workable: 15-18 min walk or short rideshare | Also fine, because host covers the library-to-east transfer | Breakfast included; coffee, mini-fridge, microwave listed | Standard king; casual dinner options nearby | Free-cancel deadline remains Feb. 21; adds a little bag/logistics time Thursday but does not force a later flight if debrief ends near noon |

My read: Hampton saves about $122 before breakfast value, and the host rideshare removes the biggest disadvantage for the east-side partner visit.
Can you double-check the Hampton room basics? I need a real one-bed room, and I do care about the refrigerator and coffee maker on this one.

For the Hampton listing I have: standard king room, one king bed, in-room coffee maker, mini-fridge, microwave, and included breakfast. For Hotel Revival: standard queen is one queen bed, coffee is listed, but I would want to confirm the refrigerator/mini-fridge because it is less clearly stated than Hampton.
What about dinner without a car on Tuesday night? I may get in, answer emails, and not want to think very hard.

Hotel Revival is stronger for on-site dining because you can stay in the building. Hampton is still easy, just less self-contained: there are casual Inner Harbor and downtown options within a few blocks, plus delivery if weather is ugly. If the priority is one-step dinner, Revival wins; if the priority is total value and breakfast, Hampton wins.
If Hampton means extra rideshares, does the savings mostly disappear?

Not really. Roughly:

| Cost item | Revival | Hampton |
|---|---:|---:|
| Room total | ~$438 | ~$316 |
| Extra local rideshares tied to hotel location | ~$0-10 | ~$18-30 if you ride instead of walking Wed/Thu morning |
| Breakfast value over 2 mornings | Not included | Saves roughly $25-40 |

Even after a couple of short rideshares, Hampton is likely still $100+ better in practical value. The trade-off is convenience: Revival is simpler for the 9:00 start and for retrieving bags Thursday.
So is the cheaper Hampton worth the slightly less convenient location, or would you keep the library one?

I would switch to Hampton unless the Thursday debrief is likely to run past 12:30. The 9:00 meeting is still easy with a short rideshare or a planned walk, the host covers the awkward afternoon transfer, and the breakfast plus clearer in-room setup make the lower total defensible. Keep Revival only if you want maximum no-thinking logistics and on-site dinner more than the savings.
Okay, let's use Hampton and release the library hold. Keep the United 2:40 return as the working flight, but don't ticket until the debrief end time is firm. Please add a note about bags on Thursday.

Done. Baltimore lodging is now Hampton Inner Harbor, Feb. 22-24, standard king, about $316 total, breakfast included, with in-room coffee, mini-fridge, and microwave listed. I’ll mark the Hotel Revival/library-area hold to release before tomorrow’s 6 p.m. deadline.

For Thursday: either bring your bag to the debrief if the host allows it, or leave enough time to retrieve it from Hampton before heading to BWI. The United 2:40 p.m. return stays workable if the debrief ends around noon; if it moves later than about 12:30, we should recheck flight timing before ticketing.
